method: First review by this reviewer; all 25 cited actual 1800×1013 source page images inspected before independently solving 37 revision items. Author keys, solutions and previous review findings were not read.

answers.reasoning: The first bullet names dynamic systems, computer science and domain ontology. Each other option replaces one member with a related but unlisted field.

The slide says to retain the aspects affecting the investigated performance, not every physical detail. It explicitly links omitted less-important effects to efficiency/usability while retaining meaningful predictions. Both statements are true and the reason supplies the explanation.

p130 classifies continuous models by their time representation/differential equations. p138 uses differential equations for continuous simulation; p139 explicitly says computers simulate continuous systems with discrete steps. The numerical sampling does not change the underlying modeled continuous dynamics into a different physical model.

p142 defines resolution as detail, including individual refresh rates, and fidelity as match to reality. p143 explicitly allows more detail without more accuracy. Bad noise calibration can prevent fidelity improvement despite the increased resolution; scenario scale need not change.

p144 distinguishes implementation verification from intended-use agreement with reality and gives this exact 30-degree flip example. The failure is a validation mismatch for the stated use, not proof of a syntax error, and successful code verification does not guarantee physical validity.

The actual photograph has a lower-right arrow and label Carrier board with I/O ports. The separate upper label locates the Orin Nano compute module below the heat sink. Heat sink, compute module and an external board are not the named carrier-board answer.

The printed three bullets order initial boot/VS Code, virtual environment with required packages, and then programs. The revised options make recognizable prerequisite-order mistakes rather than assuming generic setup can always precede boot.

The two printed alternatives are SD Card Image Method and NVIDIA SDK Manager Method. The first is explicitly preferred for simple/easy setup; a package update is not listed as an initial flashing method.

The editor instruction explicitly says arm64 .deb and the interpreter line says select the created virtual environment. AMD64, rpm and the unrelated system interpreter each break one specified requirement.

The right-hand list names an isolated Python environment, separate interpreter, project-specific packages and avoiding dependency conflicts. It does not promise permanent version freezing or global synchronized upgrades. This is package/interpreter-context isolation, not an OS security sandbox.

p155 says RVC3 is built on roboticstoolbox and machinevisiontoolbox, which depend on NumPy, SciPy and matplotlib.pyplot. p169 supplies general package-use context, not a reversed dependency graph. Only the stated outward dependency chain matches.

The shown q and offset arrays both contain four entries; addition is elementwise and gives [0.15,-0.45,1.25,0.85]. Compatibility, not arbitrary unequal shapes, governs broadcasting; neither concatenation nor matrix multiplication describes this code.

The phase-portrait box names stream plots, attractors and stability regions; the line-plot box names joint/control signals over time. State-space flow is different from a time-history or frequency-response curve.

The actual boxes pair 3D trajectories with ax.plot3D, matrix/grid visualization with sns.heatmap or plt.imshow, and animation with FuncAnimation. The wrong mappings exchange operations with different representations.

The Bode box explicitly attributes bode_plot to python-control. sns.heatmap is the Seaborn-style namespace while plt.imshow is the Matplotlib option. The page title does not assign every named utility to matplotlib.pyplot.

The code reads the CSV, converts timestamp values with pd.to_datetime(...,unit="s"), then sets time as the index. Using raw seconds, millisecond units, or sorting by position breaks the displayed time interpretation.

The division operator ends a physical line outside any open parentheses and without a backslash. Python must parse the entire file before executing its statements, so a literal transcription raises SyntaxError before CSV reading or data processing. Independent compile/exec confirmed no prior sentinel line executed.

Finite differences are 0.02/0.02=1, 0.04/0.02=2 and 0.06/0.02=3 m/s. The first row is undefined because it has no predecessor and is not one of the three requested defined velocities. Executed with the explicitly generated data and repaired syntax.

The four table rows respectively align/change sensor sampling, compute sliding-window statistics, aggregate groups, and synchronize/combine related tables. These are distinct operations; swapping the middle or boundary roles is incorrect.

The two-column selection is followed by describe(), assigned to summary and printed. The export call is df.to_csv("cleaned_joints.csv"), so it writes the DataFrame, not the statistics object. A generated in-memory DataFrame/export check confirmed this without needing the unseen CSV.

The function definition creates compute_distance, but the later call asks for compute_travel_distance. With the explicit fresh-namespace premise, name lookup fails first with NameError; argument binding, attribute lookup and local-variable access are not reached. Independent execution confirms it.

At 0.5, reading<0.5 is false, so the STOP/break block is skipped. reading<1.0 is true, setting Reduce speed; continue then prevents the later forward branch. This is a supplied boundary variant, not a claim about the printed list.
At 1.0, both strict less-than tests are false. The else attached to the second if selects MOVE_FORWARD. Equality does not cause a Python comparison error or leave the action unset.

The shown move computes distance=1.5*4=6.0 and prints the message, but has no return statement. Assignment receives None, not the local number or the printed string. Independent execution confirms rover_1 moved 6.0 meters and None.

Both child declarations inherit Robot and override only move. Their constructors therefore use the inherited Robot.__init__(self,name,speed), storing the attributes before any move call. Independently instantiated both classes.

The imports and commentary identify NumPy arrays, scipy.spatial.distance.euclidean, and matplotlib.pyplot plotting. The latter page actually calls euclidean and plt.plot/plt.scatter, distinguishing the ownerships.

The four movement segments have lengths sqrt(2),sqrt(1.25),sqrt(1.25),sqrt(2). Their sum is 2sqrt(2)+sqrt(5)=5.064495102..., rounding to 5.064 coordinate units. The final position is (4,3), so 5 is displacement and sqrt(2) is remaining goal distance, not path length.

The array of all four motions is floating dtype because it contains 0.5, hence even motions[0]=[1.0,1.0] is floating. The initial pose is integer. An in-place add cannot store this floating ufunc output in the integer array with same_kind casting, so it fails on the first row; the original rebinding pose=pose+m would work. Independently reproduced the UFuncTypeError under NumPy 2.3.5.

The second summary row explicitly names NumPy, SciPy, Matplotlib and Pandas. SymPy, Seaborn and Numba appear in other roles but do not replace members of this named four-library stack. The numeric 90% claim is correctly not generalized.
The performance row pairs vectorization/NumPy, JIT/Numba, GPU arrays/CuPy or JAX, and parallelism/Ray. Each incorrect mapping swaps named approaches and tools.

The ROS 2 rclpy row calls it a bridge between Python simulation and real hardware. It is not itself the dynamics integrator, a visualization-only interface, or an RL training algorithm. The assumption properly avoids guaranteeing universal unchanged-code portability.

The final row names parameter identification, domain randomization and validation against physical measurements. Simulation-only fitting, prettier plots and ignoring physical comparison do not establish real-world correspondence.

The lower-left scipy.linalg box explicitly says Advanced linear algebra, LAPACK wrappers. FFTW and ODEPACK name other algorithm families; the no-higher-level-solver claim is incompatible with the named wrappers.

The heatmap/matrix box lists confusion matrices, cost-to-go grids and occupancy maps. Therefore choose o1 (confusion matrices and occupancy maps) and o2 (cost-to-go grids); Bode curves and connected 3D paths belong to different boxes.

The real-time animation box explicitly gives FuncAnimation plus blitting. A complete redraw is not the named optimization, and the stem correctly avoids turning the printed 30+ fps into a universal guarantee.

The resample row explicitly uses the 50 Hz IMU versus 200 Hz encoder example. rolling is a sliding statistic, describe a summary, and to_csv an export. Changing sample alignment does not create extra independently measured information.

The scipy.optimize row explicitly includes PID auto-tuning and system identification with inverse kinematics. Integration, signal filtering and spatial geometry correspond to distinct SciPy families, not the requested extra optimize uses.
